label: Climate & disturbance
blurb: Recent fire, projected climate exposure and sea-level rise: how much of the 30x30 network they touch, and how much of each lies in 30x30.

headlines.label: 30x30 network in 5 ft sea-level rise zone

charts.title: Climate and disturbance features
charts.subtitle: Share of each feature's extent in this area by conservation status

method: Burned area is every CAL FIRE fire perimeter from 2015 on (the report's 'past decade'), on resolution-10 cells; statewide this gives 13.9% of the 30x30 network burned (report: 14%). Climate exposure is Thorne et al. (2016) for mid-century, natural vegetation only (CWHR major-habitat classes other than agriculture and urban), with a mean exposure index of 0.9 or more on resolution-9 cells counted as exposed, separately for the MIROC5 and CNRM-CM5 models. The report does not state its cutoff; this one reproduces its extents (MIROC5 25.5 vs 26.7 million acres, CNRM-CM5 27.9 vs 28.5 million), its shares in 30x30 (32.7% vs 31.7%, 30.0% vs 29.8%) and its finding that about 32% of the network is projected to be climate-stressed (31.4% and 31.6% here). Sea-level rise is NOAA's 5-foot inundation layer, which includes existing open water and so does not match the report's extent (tracked in ca-30x30#104). The report publishes no need classes for these features.
